title: Airbyte Records-Synced Volume Anomaly
dataSources: Fivetran log-service events and REST API (`connectors`, sync status), Airbyte job logs (`airbyte:job`), Matillion task history, Kafka Connect connector/task status, AWS Glue job runs (CloudWatch), ADF pipeline runs (Azure Monitor).
app: Fivetran / Airbyte / Stitch / Matillion logs and REST APIs via HEC scripted inputs; Kafka Connect JMX/REST; cloud ELT via `Splunk_TA_aws` (Glue) and `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (ADF).
spl:
index=dataops sourcetype=airbyte:job event=job_completed status=succeeded
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(records_synced) as rows by connection_name, _time
| eventstats avg(rows) as avg_rows, stdev(rows) as sd_rows by connection_name
| eval z=round((rows-avg_rows)/sd_rows,2)
| where abs(z)>3
| sort - _time
description: Baselines the daily record count per Airbyte connection and flags sudden jumps or drops, a classic sign of an upstream schema or filter change.
value: A sync that succeeds but moves a fraction of the usual rows is a silent data-loss bug; volume anomaly detection catches what a pass/fail check misses.
implementation: Ingest job completion events with record counts; schedule daily; tune the z-score threshold; investigate anomalies.
visualization: Table of anomalies by z-score, volume trend per connection.
grandmaExplanation: We learn how much data normally arrives each day and flag sudden jumps or drops, which often mean something upstream changed.
